summary: A 20-level holder leaves while a 5-level holder stays, and comes back on the same deeper socket: the book from before it left is not its own, so it gets the main feed's 5-level book until the socket's next one.

notes: Review F1 (lead's review-2): a deep book is the holder's own only while its socket's session is current and something holds the instrument at those levels (feed/bridge/snapshot.rs forget_deep_book, forget_deep_session).

deviations.reason: The web sends every Depth holder of an instrument both books, the 5-level one and the 20-level one in turn; the desktop sends a 5-level holder only the 5-level book.

The web sends Dhan's trade time in epoch seconds as ltt; feed timestamps are epoch milliseconds (docs/prompt/websockets-format.md). The 20-level frame's ltt is that same value, from the instrument's latest quote (the web's 20-level frame has none).
A depth frame keeps ltp, which the SDK's Depth callback reads: 0 before the instrument's first quote, its last traded price after; the web's 20-level frame has no ltp.

A 20-level packet has no totals, so the book frame takes them from the instrument's latest quote on the market feed (1.0.6 decision, kept: the depth frame carries the latest quote); before any quote they are left out, as on the web.

The day's OI high and low came with the last full packet. They are market state: later packets that do not carry them leave them standing on the depth frame, and a new market connection starts them afresh. The web sends them only in a full packet's own dict, and its 20-level frame has neither.
